newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Mine blast kills three Bosnian youths.
newsitem.headline: Mine blast kills three Bosnian youths.

text.p: Three Bosnian teenagers were killed when a mine exploded on Sunday in a Sarajevo suburb, police and NATO officers said.
Bosnian authorities said the blast took place in the village of Sovrle in Ilijas suburb, west of the city centre, in Bosnia's Moslem-Croat federation.
"They were killed in a minefield," said Major Tony White, spokesman for the NATO-led peace force in Bosnia.
Police identified the victims as teenagers, including a brother and sister who were refugees from the eastern town of Visegrad.

Bosnia is littered with several million mines after four years of war in former Yugoslavia. Rival armies have been slow to fulfil promises to remove the mines while continuing to produce them in their arms factories.
The International Committee of the Red Cross fears mine injuries will rise in 1997 as memories of the war fade and farmers begin spring planting near former front lines.
